old: they all made an excellent dinner
new: they all had an excellent dinner
reason: False friend: 'make dinner' now means to cook it; Butler's idiom means to eat it.

old: by the treachery of Aegisthus and his wife
new: by the treachery of Aegisthus and of his own wife
reason: Reader misread 'his' as Aegisthus's. Butler (and the Greek reflexive) mean Agamemnon's own wife. The adjudicator proposed 'his own wife'; the lead adds 'of' so the two agents are separate and 'his own' binds to Agamemnon.
Hidden agent: in Butler the subject carries over from 'Jove … made it blow hard'. The reader took Menelaus to be the one dividing the fleet and was contradicted by the next sentences.
Dead sense: 'substance' meaning property. A listed prior example.

old: among people of an alien speech
new: among people of a foreign tongue
reason: A listed prior example, ruled on in context. Butler's 'of an alien speech' (Greek: of strange speech) is an archaic construction. Read aloud, 'alien' now suggests extraterrestrial or estranged. The adjudicator kept it; the lead renders the construction plainly, keeping 'tongue' for register. Butler's ¶23 has no other 'tongue' or 'spoke'. Final wording follows independent verification R1: it mirrors the edition's rendering of the same Greek word at 1.13 ('men of a foreign tongue').
